THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT  AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:09.10.2012  -2-  MFA No. 7036 of 2019 PASSED IN MVC NO. 132/2011 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE JMFC & MACT, PANDAVAPURA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.10,18,379/- awarded by the Tribunal, is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.

3. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
1. Contaminated open wound on right knee with comminuted fracture of lower end of right femur and upper end of tibia with neuro vascular injury.
2. Tear of lower lip,
3. Tear of right ear.
4. Cut lacerated wound on right frontal region.
5. Tenderness over right hand.
4. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation:

This is a case, in which the claimant suffered an amputation above the knee.
Though the doctor had assessed the disability at 100%, the Tribunal has determined the disability at 50% to the whole body.
In my view, having regard the claimant had 19 years old and he has suffered an amputation of his leg above the knee, it would be appropriate to determine the disability at 80%.
6. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.3,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2011, would be Rs.6,500/-.

7. As the claimant had suffered disability at 80% to the whole body and was aged 19 years, it would be appropriate to consider 40% towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.9,100/-.
8. As the claimant was aged 19 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.15,72,480/- (9,100 x 12 x 18 x 80%) towards 'loss of future income'.
9.
The sums awarded by the Tribunal on the other heads are just and proper and the same do not call for modification and hence confirmed.
10. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified only in respect of loss of future earning and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.22,66,859/- as against Rs.10,18,379/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
12. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
13. The claimant would not be entitled for the interest on the compensation for the delayed period of 2362 days in filing the appeal.
14. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
15. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
